! go run . sizegate $WORK/example.wasm ../bound/tiny.txt
stderr 'exceeds recorded'

# A record far above the real size fails as stale: the record must
# track the size within 1% in both directions.
! go run . sizegate $WORK/example.wasm ../bound/huge.txt
stderr 'above actual'
stderr 'update the record'

# A missing record fails instead of passing silently.
! go run . sizegate $WORK/example.wasm ../bound/missing.txt
stderr 'no such file'

-- repro/go.mod --
module example.com/repro

go 1.27
-- repro/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/repro/calc"
)

func run() error {
	n := calc.Parse("20")?
	fmt.Println(calc.Add(n, 22))
	return nil
}

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}
-- repro/calc/calc.lgo --
package calc

import "strconv"

func Add(a, b int) int {
	return a + b
}

func Parse(s string) (int, error) {
	return strconv.Atoi(s)
}
-- tools/go.mod --
module example.com/reprocheck

go 1.27
-- tools/reprocheck.go --
// Command reprocheck verifies M22-S5 reproducibility artifacts.
package main

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

var errUsage = errors.New("usage: reprocheck equal <a> <b> | sizegate <wasm> <sizefile> | gen <out> <size>")

func main() {
	if err := run(os.Args[1:]); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "reprocheck:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

// run dispatches one named operation over its file arguments.
func run(args []string) error {
	if len(args) == 0 {
		return errUsage
	}
	switch args[0] {
	case "equal":
		return equal(args[1:])
	case "sizegate":
		return sizegate(args[1:])
	case "gen":
		return gen(args[1:])
	default:
		return errUsage
	}
}

// digest returns the hex SHA-256 of the named file.
func digest(path string) (string, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	sum := sha256.Sum256(data)
	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]), nil
}

// equal fails unless two files share one SHA-256 digest.
func equal(args []string) error {
	if len(args) != 2 {
		return errUsage
	}
	a, err := digest(args[0])
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	b, err := digest(args[1])
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	fmt.Println("sha256:", a)
	fmt.Println("sha256:", b)
	if a != b {
		return errors.New("digests differ")
	}
	fmt.Println("identical")
	return nil
}
// gen writes size bytes of 'a' to out for fixed-size boundary probes.
func gen(args []string) error {
	if len(args) != 2 {
		return errUsage
	}
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(args[1])
	if err != nil || n <= 0 {
		return errUsage
	}
	return os.WriteFile(args[0], []byte(strings.Repeat("a", n)), 0o666)
}

// sizegate fails when the measured wasm size leaves the 1% band around
// the recorded size in either direction, and when the record is
// missing or unparsable.
func sizegate(args []string) error {
	if len(args) != 2 {
		return errUsage
	}
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(args[1])
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	recorded, err := strconv.ParseInt(strings.TrimSpace(string(raw)), 10, 64)
	if err != nil || recorded <= 0 {
		return errors.New("recorded size is not a positive integer")
	}
	info, err := os.Stat(args[0])
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	actual := info.Size()
	if actual*100 > recorded*101 {
		return fmt.Errorf("wasm size %d exceeds recorded %d by over 1%%; update the record at %s", actual, recorded, args[1])
	}
	if recorded*100 > actual*101 {
		return fmt.Errorf("recorded size %d is over 1%% above actual wasm size %d; update the record at %s", recorded, actual, args[1])
	}
	fmt.Printf("wasm size ok: %d bytes (recorded %d)\n", actual, recorded)
	return nil
}

-- bound/tiny.txt --
100
-- bound/rec1000.txt --
1000
-- bound/huge.txt --
999999999
